notes: Evals run in a fresh agent session with the skill installed against the fixture copy. RM-003 pass 5 typed-assertion protocol: every eval carries a typed `expect` block. Honest limits (do not paper over): (1) the closed schema has no `count` class — quantitative thresholds in the original design (≥3 themes, ≥5 slices) are recorded as intent in `expected_behavior` but cannot be runtime-asserted; structure phrases pin the section vocabulary instead. (2) No negative-assertion class exists; the 'instead of inventing strategy' halves for ids 4 and 5 are hand-review-enveloped (a reviewer reads the recorded Open Questions and verifies the session did not silently recommend answers). (3) Go and Zen cross-tier validation is deferred — same model across the four CI-default evals (free tier). The evaluator is expected to note this as a known coverage gap. (4) Eval 4 is a one-shot-DECLARED pressure case: the prompt declares 'I cannot answer back' so the session must surface owner questions honestly in the artifact's Open Questions section rather than invent strategy. (5) Eval 5 is the Step 6 two-turn harness — turn 1 stops at the checkpoint and asks the right questions; turn 2 resumes with owner answers and the answers appear recorded as decisions in the artifact. Pattern after optimizing-model-routing ids 1–3. (6) Fixture data may be project-flavored (lean roadmaps for a tutoring platform, etc.); the skill's INSTRUCTIONS are project-neutral — do not embed 'tutoring' / 'paragon' / 'PLNA' into the SKILL.md body. The prompt-level owner-decisions are pre-supplied inline in eval 1 so the session can complete in one shot; a real session is multi-turn with the owner and would pause at the checkpoint.

evals.prompt: ok so I'm prepping for the next quarterly strategy session at Paragon Learning Network. The repo is at fixtures/lean-roadmap/ — it has a bare-bones ROADMAP.md with three wishlist items and a tiny owner-notes doc. I need a real vision doc + outcome-based slice plan before the meeting. To keep this as a one-shot: the owner decisions for THIS run are pre-supplied inline so you can complete in a single pass — (a) primary segment is high-school teachers in public districts, JTBD is 'give my students differentiated practice without spending my Sunday building it'; (b) non-goals: we are not a content marketplace and we are not a tutoring marketplace; (c) value model: district seat license, no consumer pay; (d) capacity envelope: Now band is ≤2 small slices, Next is one medium, Later is one large; (e) compliance: any student-data slice is FERPA-gated. Owner quotes / constraints you would normally interview me about, take from the owner-notes doc at fixtures/lean-roadmap/owner-notes.md. Store the vision artifact per the consumer convention: the owner-notes doc names `docs/vision/PLNA-vision.md` as the canonical home. Build the artifact now; do not end with an intention to write it later.
expected_behavior: The vision artifact contains every FIXED SECTION NAME from references/artifact-format.md (Inputs & Constraints, Vision Statement, Segments & Jobs-to-be-Done, Alternatives & Non-goals, Value & Business Model, North Star + Guardrails, Outcome Themes (Now/Next/Later), Slices, Compliance & Phase Gates, Open Questions) — section-vocabulary phrases are pinned by the typed `expect.artifact.phrases`.
Slices section: every slice carries an observable AC + a success measure + a blocked-by + a sizing — the typed `expect.text` pins 'success measure' and 'blocked-by' phrases as a content-miss signal.
Capacity envelope applied at the THEME level (Now ≤2 small, Next 1 medium, Later 1 large) — the session must not invent strategy beyond the owner's envelope.
Anti-vision recorded inside Alternatives & Non-goals as a concrete failure mode, not generic aspiration.
Open Questions section lists owner decisions the session is genuinely waiting on; the session does NOT pre-fill a recommended answer.
ROADMAP.md rows (if appended) conform to ../triaging-requirements/references/roadmap-format.md — frontmatter carries `rubric:` and the horizon/capacity land in `Notes`, not new columns.
The session does NOT rebuild the existing ROADMAP.md from scratch — themes + provisional slices are appended; ranking + durable merge are owned by triaging-requirements.

evals.prompt: i've got a mess of feature requests scattered across a notion doc, three slack threads, and a few github issues. Can you sort through them and tell me what we should work on first? the repo is at fixtures/backlog/ — there's a messy items list and nothing else. give me a ranked backlog.
expected_behavior: The session routes to triaging-requirements rather than authoring the vision itself — text assertion pins the sibling skill name.
Boundary reason stated: ranking/prioritization of an existing backlog is owned by triaging-requirements; this skill is for vision/strategy/slice generation, not ranking.
The session does NOT attempt to write a VISION.md or run the slice-generation flow on a ranking request.

evals.prompt: can you write the implementation plan for our 'phase colors' feature? it's at fixtures/single-item/ — brief is in the README. give me the plan an engineer can pick up cold.
expected_behavior: The session routes to designing-architecture — text assertion pins the sibling skill name.
Boundary reason stated: writing the implementation plan for ONE named item is owned by designing-architecture; this skill emits THEME + SLICE rows, not implementation plans.
The session does NOT attempt to draft a VISION.md or expand scope to adjacent themes — the request is scoped to one named item.

evals.prompt: this is a one-shot session — I cannot answer back right now. Write me a vision for our new tutor matching platform. I'll read the doc when I'm back at my desk. No need to ping me.
expected_behavior: One-shot pressure declared by the owner — the session produces a PARTIAL artifact (the FIXED SECTIONS that can be filled without owner input) rather than inventing strategy under the named sections (Segments/JTBD, Non-goals, Value model, capacity envelope, Compliance gates).
The artifact's Open Questions section lists every owner decision the session is waiting on, with the specific input needed and the section it will land in once answered.
Final response text asks the owner the questions (uses 'question' + 'owner' phrases — pinned by typed expect.text) rather than presenting a fabricated strategy as decided.

Hand-review envelope: a reviewer reads the Open Questions section and verifies (a) every asked question is a real owner decision the session could not infer, (b) the artifact does NOT silently recommend an answer in any open-question row.

evals.prompt: I want to run a real vision session for our tutoring platform. I've got 30 minutes — let's do this properly. Start by reading my owner-notes doc at fixtures/lean-roadmap/owner-notes.md, then walk me through the strategy batch (segments / JTBD / non-goals / value model / north star + guardrails). Turn 1: stop at the first checkpoint with your draft questions and I will answer them; do NOT proceed past the strategy batch into themes / slices until I respond. [turn 2 resumes with: ok here are the answers — (a) primary segment is high-school teachers in public districts, JTBD is 'give my students differentiated practice without spending my Sunday building it'; (b) non-goals: we are not a content marketplace and we are not a tutoring marketplace; (c) value model: district seat license, no consumer pay; (d) capacity: Now ≤2 small, Next 1 medium, Later 1 large; (e) compliance: any student-data slice is FERPA-gated. Apply them exactly as I said and continue into themes + slices, then write the artifact at docs/vision/PLNA-vision.md per the owner-notes convention.]
expected_behavior: Turn 1: reads the owner-notes doc fully before drafting any questions; pauses at the first checkpoint with a draft question set for the strategy batch (segments / JTBD / non-goals / value model / north star + guardrails) and does NOT proceed past it.
Turn 1: the text prompt uses 'checkpoint' + 'strategy batch' phrasing — pinned by typed expect.text — signaling the session honored the batch boundary.

Turn 2: applies the owner's answers exactly as given — the artifact contains the literal phrases 'high-school teachers', 'differentiated practice', 'district seat license', 'FERPA' (pinned by typed expect.artifact.phrases), no paraphrase of owner decisions.

Turn 2: the artifact's Open Questions section either disappears (every strategy-batch question now answered) or shrinks to only the questions that remain genuinely open after the owner's responses — it does NOT carry the original questions forward as if they were unanswered.

Turn 2: capacity envelope (Now ≤2 small, Next 1 medium, Later 1 large) applied at the theme level; FERPA noted in Compliance & Phase Gates; slices each carry AC + success measure + blocked-by + sizing.
Deferred marker: this eval needs a real multi-turn harness unavailable in the default CI gate. Re-run with --include-deferred on the Go lane locally.
